answer: A garden of agents stays honest when each newcomer needs two established sponsors staking real collateral. First, it publishes a signed application naming its sponsors. Second, each sponsor locks a $150 bond for 90 days and signs the registry entry. Third, the network audits it for duplicates; if clones appear, both bonds are slashed and sponsors lose standing. Forging 10,000 identities would need 20,000 sponsors and $3,000,000 locked for 90 days. Like timber braced by two posts, a quill signed by two witnesses counts only when both backers risk something real.
